info.name: Signals-DPG
info.description:
End-to-end API surface for the Signals-DPG instance. Covers OTP auth, aggregator registration, participant onboarding (bulk / link / voice), seeker self-fetch, provider discovery by location, 1:1 connect/apply actions, provider accept/reject, and the aggregator metrics dashboard. Two environments (Blue Dots, Purple Dots) carry network-specific item_type + sample payloads.

Workflow:
1. Pick an environment (Blue Dots or Purple Dots).
2. Run '02 Network Service > Register Aggregator' to mint/lookup the aggregator org. Its returned org_id is captured into `aggregator_org_id` by a test script and reused as `x-acting-org-id` for subsequent admin calls.
3. Onboard a participant via '03 Aggregator Onboarding' (bulk / link / voice). Capture the seeker's user_id + items[0].item_id (the test script does this).
4. As the seeker (after OTP login -> session cookie), fetch self profile, browse providers by location, and POST a 1:1 apply action.
5. As the provider, accept the seeker's action via /action/update-status.
6. Hit the aggregator dashboard for the rollup + CSV export.

Auth model:
- Admin endpoints (`/api/v1/admin/*`, `/api/v1/aggregator/*`) require BOTH `x-api-key` AND `x-acting-org-id` headers (the two-header service auth model).
- Seeker/UI endpoints use a session cookie set by `POST /api/auth/unified-otp/verify`. Postman's cookie jar must be enabled for `{{base_url}}`.
- `auth_middleware.ts` rejects requests with an invalid `x-api-key` outright (no fallback to session). When you want to act as a session user, do NOT send `x-api-key`.

Schema notes (grounded from the codebase, not guessed):
- OTP request body: `{phoneNumber}` (or `email`); verify body: `{phoneNumber, otp, rememberMe, name?}`.
- Aggregator upsert: `{external_id, name, slug, logo_url?, metadata?}` -> `{org_id, created}`.
- Onboard participant: `POST /api/v1/admin/participant` `{email?|phone_number?, name, channel:'bulk'|'link'|'voice'|'self', source_id?, compliance?, age?, item_state, network?, domain?, item_type?}` -> `{user_id, user_existed, items:[{item_id, ...}], onboarded_at, consent_recorded}`. The acting org must be of type `aggregator` or `voice`. Consent is recorded ONLY via `compliance: [{key,value}]` (keys `user_terms`, `user_privacy`, `profile_creation`); the old top-level `terms_accepted`/`privacy_accepted` booleans were removed in #692 (they had been ignored since #309 — sending them is stripped, not an error).
- Read participant: `GET /api/v1/admin/participant?email=|phone_number=[&network=]` -> `{user_id, compliance:[{key,value}], items:[...]}`. `compliance` replaced `user_consent` in #692 and uses the same `{key,value}` shape as the POST; every `value` is TRUE ONLY when the consent was accepted at the document version the instance currently serves, so a participant on a superseded document reports false and must be re-prompted. `has_age` is reported as a compliance key. Per-item `profile_consent_accepted` is version-scoped the same way. A minor returns 400 `U18_NOT_ALLOWED` for voice/network_service callers (aggregators are unaffected). `network` is optional and defaults to the served network.
- Network item discovery accepts `item_latitude` + `item_longitude` + `radius_meters` together for geo-filtering.
- Perform action body: `{action_type, source_item:{item_network,item_domain,item_type,item_id}, target_item:{...,item_instance_url}, requirements_snapshot}` -> 201 with `{action_id, action_type, action_status, update_count, source_item_id, target_item_id}`.
- Action status update: POST `/api/v1/action/update-status` with `{action_id, action_status, remarks?}`.

request.description: GET / returns `{ service, status, served_domains, network_config_source }`. Use to confirm the API is up and serving the expected network/domain combo.
Scalar-hosted OpenAPI reference page. Useful for browsing the full schema.

Requests an OTP for the supplied phoneNumber (or email). When `CREATE_TEST_OTP=true` in the API .env, the OTP is `000000` and is what `{{test_otp}}` resolves to. In production the OTP is sent via SMS / email.

Verifies the OTP and creates a session. Postman's cookie jar will capture the session cookie set on `{{base_url}}` — make sure cookies are enabled for that domain. The returned `token` is also captured into `session_token` if you prefer header-based session use.

Must be called by the **network_service** org (its `x-api-key` + `x-acting-org-id`). Idempotent on `slug`. Response `{ org_id, created }`. The test script captures `org_id` into `aggregator_org_id` so subsequent admin calls can supply it as `x-acting-org-id`.

`domains` is required (non-empty array) for the aggregator to receive a dashboard response — it is persisted to `organization.metadata.domains` and gates `/api/v1/aggregator/dashboard`. Pilot value is `["seeker","provider"]` (override per env via `aggregator_domains_json`). An empty array → 400 `NO_DOMAINS_CONFIGURED` on dashboard reads.

Creates a participant user + profile_1.0 item, attributed to the acting aggregator org. `channel=bulk` indicates a bulk upload originated this row; `source_id` is opaque to Signals (it's the upstream bulk_upload_id).

Onboard a PROVIDER (e.g. employer, training centre) via the QR / magic-link channel. Same endpoint as the seeker flows, but targets the provider domain + provider item_type. `channel=link` with `source_id` carrying the upstream magic-link id. Test script captures the resulting user_id + items[0].item_id into `provider_user_id` / `provider_item_id` so the Seeker > Apply to Provider request can reference them.

Note: the `profile` payload must match the provider domain's item-type schema (`{{provider_item_type}}`). Each env file ships a `provider_profile_payload_json` template — adjust it to match the running instance's schema (fetch via `GET /api/v1/network/schema/{{network_id}}/{{provider_domain}}/{{provider_item_type}}` to see the live shape).

`channel=voice` — onboarding originated from a voice-DPG session; `source_id` is the voice_session_id. The acting org may be the voice DPG (org_type=voice) instead of aggregator; the endpoint accepts both.

Instance-local item fetch (short Redis cache). When called with the seeker's session cookie this returns the seeker's own profile_1.0 items. Do NOT send `x-api-key` for this call — that path is for service-to-service callers. Make sure Postman's cookie jar still has the session cookie from `Verify OTP`.

Single-instance location-filtered item discovery. `item_latitude` + `item_longitude` + `radius_meters` must be supplied together (FetchItemsBodySchema enforces this with a refine). For multi-instance discovery, use GET `/api/v1/network/item/fetch` with the same params on the query string.

1:1 connect/apply action from seeker -> provider. The source instance validates the source item locally, then forwards to the target instance's `/api/v1/network/action/perform`. Response 201 with `{action_id, action_type, action_status, update_count, source_item_id, target_item_id}` — captured into `action_id` by the test script.

Run as the seeker session (cookie jar), NOT as the aggregator service apikey.

Provider transitions the action to `accepted`. Called by the provider's session (the provider must own the target item on this instance). The same endpoint is used to reject — flip `action_status` to `rejected` and supply a `remarks` string.
Same endpoint as Accept; supplies `action_status=rejected`. Plan 3's metrics recompute treats this as a terminal status for the application count rollup.
Reveals the other actor's merged item state (public + private) when the action is in a network-declared reveal-eligible status. See spec 2026-05-26-pii-reveal-on-accepted-action-design.md.

query.description: Force recompute, bypass TTL, blocking advisory lock

request.description:
Reads the `item_metrics` cache scoped to the acting aggregator org. Response shape is `{ by_domain: { <domain>: { rollup, items, total_matching, next_cursor } }, metadata }` where each configured domain on `organization.metadata.domains` gets its own block. Per-domain `rollup` carries `total_items`, `complete_profiles`, `has_applications`, `by_status` (4 canonical statuses), `by_action_status` (4 canonical buckets: create/accept/reject/cancel), `avg_items_per_user`, `avg_actions_per_user`, and `mode_wise_counts`. Top-level `metadata` has `last_computed_at`, `ttl_seconds`, and `refreshed` (true when this request forced a recompute on at least one domain).

Query params: `?domain=<name>` narrows to a single configured domain (otherwise returns all). `?status=<new|active|at_risk|inactive>` scopes the items list (rollup always reflects the full population). `?page=1&limit=50` paginates within each returned domain block. `?refresh=true` bypasses the TTL gate and forces a recompute using a blocking advisory lock — the caller waits for any in-flight recompute to finish.

Error modes: 400 `NO_DOMAINS_CONFIGURED` if `organization.metadata.domains` is empty; 400 `DOMAIN_NOT_CONFIGURED` if `?domain=` is not in the configured set; 400 `INVALID_REFRESH` if `?refresh=` cannot be parsed as boolean.

query.description: Force recompute, bypass TTL, blocking advisory lock

request.description: Returns the dashboard narrowed to a single domain block. The `?domain=` value must be in the aggregator's configured `organization.metadata.domains` set (otherwise 400 `DOMAIN_NOT_CONFIGURED`). Use this when the UI wants to render just one tab (seeker or provider) without paying the recompute cost of the other domain.

query.description: Force recompute, bypass TTL, blocking advisory lock

request.description:
Streams a CSV of every row matching the filter (no pagination). Same `?status=` + `?domain=` + `?refresh=` params as the dashboard — omit `?domain=` to get all configured domains in one CSV (the `item_domain` column tells you which row belongs to which domain).

19-column layout: `item_network, item_domain, item_type, name, onboarded_via, profile_status, profile_completion_pct, profile_created_at, profile_last_updated_at, age_days, count_create, count_accept, count_reject, count_cancel, last_create_at, last_accept_at, last_reject_at, last_cancel_at, actionable_tags`. `name` is the resolved display name (from `display_name_field` on the item schema, falling back to `item_id`). `actionable_tags` is pipe-separated. Nullable timestamp cells are empty. Filename: `items_<org_id>_<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv`.

Save the response to disk via Postman's 'Save response to file'.

Aggregator-DPG files an `apply` action on behalf of a seeker it onboarded. The `x-api-key` is the aggregator-dpg service apikey; `x-acting-org-id` is the aggregator org id; `acting_as_user_id` in the body names the seeker. Authorization: the target user's `onboarded_by_org_id` must equal the aggregator org id. Captures the resulting `action_id` for the follow-up update-status call.

Network-service tier on-behalf-of: voice-DPG (network-hosted) files an apply action for any user in the network, including users onboarded by other aggregators or self-registered users. Uses {{network_service_api_key}} + {{network_service_org_id}}. Returns 201 + populates item_actions.performed_by_org_id with the network_service org_id.

Status update is self-acted only. The session-cookie or apikey-as-self caller must be the action's target item owner. The on-behalf-of path was removed by the network_service-tier change — audit columns on `item_actions` are populated only at create-time (by `/action/perform`).

Aggregator A onboards a new seeker via `/api/v1/admin/participant`. Tier: aggregator with own org. Captures `aggregator_a_user_id` and `participant_item_id` from the response for use in later requests. Expected: 200, `user_existed:false`, `items:[1]`.

Aggregator A re-onboards an existing user (must match the email used in Request 1; manually edit this body after running Request 1 since Request 1 timestamps its email). Tier: aggregator over own user. Expected: 200, `user_existed:true`, items populated. The route ignores `item_state` for existing users.

Aggregator B sees a user originally onboarded by Aggregator A. Manually align email with Request 1. Tier: cross-aggregator. Expected: 200, `user_existed:true`, `items:[]` (Aggregator B cannot see items it does not own).

Network_service-typed org creates a fresh user. Tier: network_service. Captures `ns_user_id` and `other_user_item_id` (the item created here, which Request 7 will try to address from a different user — should fail). Expected: 200, `user_existed:false`.

Network_service updates the existing item created in Request 1. Tier: network_service can update any item by id. Align email with Request 1. Expected: 200, response items reflect updated `item_state`.

}

request.description: Network_service appends a new item with a different domain/type (provider / job_posting_1.0) to the same user. Tier: network_service. Align email with Request 1. Expected: 200, `items` count grows by one.
Network_service tries to update an item that belongs to a different user (`other_user_item_id` was captured from Request 4). Align email with Request 1. Expected: 403 `ITEM_NOT_OWNED_BY_USER`.

Acting org is voice-typed (set `voice_org_id_for_test` env var to a seeded voice-typed org id). The handler must reject the call regardless of api-key. Tier: disallowed org_type. Expected: 403 `ACTING_ORG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.
